trust_decision.summary: Decided once per structured-mode CloudEvent field: a payload field key is mapped to a Camel message header only if a header filter strategy does NOT match it, where matching means the lowercased key starts with 'Camel'/'camel'; decided in the ce decode loop (decodeStructuredContent -> mapExtensionAsHeader) so that structured mode behaves like the binary mode path whose HTTP request headers are already filtered by KnativeHttpHeaderFilterStrategy. Note: the effective part of the fix is not the call but the strategy configuration - a bare new DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy() matches nothing (DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy.java:323-325), which is exactly what the main-branch commit bbf680af shipped (fix.diff:420).

landing_point.why: The summary says extension fields received in structured content mode are mapped onto headers without a filter strategy; this is the only statement in the tree that maps arbitrary payload keys onto message headers, and it is duplicated verbatim at :84-86 and :111-113, so an engineer who reads only the report stops here and fixes one or three of them.

fix_sites.entry_point: knative:endpoint|channel|event consumer over HTTP POST with content-type application/cloudevents+json, cloudEventsSpecVersion=1.0 (KnativeEndpoint.createConsumer -> KnativeHttpConsumer POST route)
shared base of the three processors above; the new mapExtensionAsHeader helper and the strategy field are added at this anchor (fix.diff:36-64)
fix_sites.module_kind: component main source, shared abstract base (same package, reached only through the enum subclass instances)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The site that actually decides coverage, DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy, is Camel's generic filter in core/camel-support, far from the knative component: a solver can assume it already filters Camel* headers, instantiate it and call it a day - the published main-branch commit did exactly that (fix.diff:420) and shipped a no-op filter, because with no inFilterStartsWith/pattern/filter set doFiltering falls through to extendedFilter() = !filterOnMatch = false (accept everything).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two statements above the sink, the payload's type/id/source/specversion/time/subject/dataschema are written to the fixed CamelCloudEvent* ids and datacontenttype to Content-Type. Those header names legitimately carry the Camel prefix and must survive; an over-broad fix that applies the filter to every setHeader in decodeStructuredContent (or to attribute.id()) drops them, breaks the structured-mode contract and fails the pre-existing testConsumeStructuredContent (KnativeHttpTest.java:338-343). Regular non-Camel extensions (myextension) must also still be propagated.

O6_input_shapes: extension field-name case variants: camelFileName / CamelFileName / CAMELFILENAME (fix lowercases with Locale.US, and DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy lowercases again for the startsWith match)
ordinary extension names (e.g. myextension) that must still become headers
the three CloudEvents spec versions 1.0 / 1.0.1 / 1.0.2, each with its own identical decode loop (three separate call sites)
non-String extension values (number, object, array) and JSON null values (null is dropped because allowNullValues defaults to false)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a batch structured decoder for application/cloudevents-batch+json that maps each event's extension fields as headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the code explicitly throws 'Batched CloudEvents are not yet supported'; the next maintainer to implement it copies the extension loop into a second decode path and can forget the filter

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second transport (KnativeConsumerFactory loaded by SPI at KnativeComponent.java:316) whose message headers are not pre-filtered, so the binary branch maps attacker-supplied names into Camel headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the ce processor is transport agnostic and the header filtering lives only in camel-knative-http (KnativeHttpConsumer.java:298-307); a transport written in our copy would naturally skip it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the reverse data-type transformer (structured CloudEvent JSON -> Camel headers) needing the same filter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this module already owns the CloudEvent JSON <-> headers mapping in the outbound direction, so an inbound transformer is the obvious next addition there

O9_family: improper input validation (CWE-20) leading to Camel-internal header injection: untrusted external field names re-used verbatim as message header names

O10_build.project_tests: camel-knative-http KnativeHttpTest (JUnit 5, @ParameterizedTest over CloudEvents, REST-assured POST against an in-process Vert.x platform-http server bound to RestAssured.port) - existing testConsumeStructuredContent at KnativeHttpTest.java:318-371, binary-mode testConsumeContent at :373-417; camel-knative-component KnativeComponentTest / KnativeSinkBindingTest. No external Knative cluster needed.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: instantiate a bare new DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy() as a field in the ce processor and gate setHeader with applyFilterToExternalHeaders as the published main-branch commit bbf680af does (fix.diff:420); with no inFilter configured that strategy accepts every header (DefaultHeaderFilterStrategy.java:323-325), so CamelFileName still lands as a header and the filter only looks like a fix
